# Dependency inventory

Points 111 and 112. `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` is the argument for each direct dependency, written
by a person. This page is the *inventory*, generated from `package.json`,
`package-lock.json` and the installed tree, and it is the freeze: `npm run audit:inventory`
regenerates it and fails if the result differs from what is committed, so no dependency —
direct or transitive — changes version without a diff somebody has to approve.

When it fails, the change is not wrong; it is unreviewed. What it owes, in this order:

1. **Security review** — advisories (`npm run audit:deps`), what the package can reach, what it
   would gain from being compromised.
2. **Licence review** — on the allowlist in `scripts/audit.mjs`, and shippable in a closed-source
   product (`THIRD_PARTY.md`).
3. **Privacy review** — does it open a connection, and does it send anything anywhere
   (`npm run audit:egress`, `docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` §What each one does on the network).
4. **Regression test** — `npm run check && npm test && npm run audit` on the new tree.

Then `npm run inventory:update`, and commit this file with the reason in the message.

## Critical dependencies, reviewed

Every *direct* dependency, production and development, with the four things a generated table
cannot derive. A direct dependency without a row here fails the audit.

### `fastify` 5.12.1 — production

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | the HTTP server: routing, body parsing, lifecycle hooks |
| Security relevance | high — it is the trust boundary; every request reaches the application through it |
| Network behaviour | inbound only; it accepts connections and never initiates one, and has no telemetry |
| Replacement possibility | node:http plus ~400 lines of routing, validation and lifecycle we would then own |

### `libsodium-wrappers-sumo` 0.7.15 — production

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | X25519, XChaCha20-Poly1305, Argon2id, Ed25519 — the primitive set the protocol needs |
| Security relevance | critical — a defect here is a defect in every cryptographic property this project claims |
| Network behaviour | none: WASM and arithmetic, no I/O of any kind |
| Replacement possibility | none acceptable. WebCrypto lacks XChaCha20-Poly1305 and Argon2id, and hand-writing either is the mistake this project exists not to make |

### `openpgp` 6.3.1 — production

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | verifying OpenPGP signatures for the optional PGP second factor (RFC 4880 packet parsing) |
| Security relevance | high, and server-side only — it decides whether a signature over a login challenge is valid |
| Network behaviour | none in this codebase: it is handed bytes already in memory, never a key-server URL |
| Replacement possibility | shelling out to `gpg`, which trades a dependency for a subprocess and a parser of its output |

### `pg` 8.23.0 — production

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | the PostgreSQL driver, for deployments that set DB_DIALECT=postgres |
| Security relevance | high — it carries every query, and the parameter binding that keeps SQL injection out |
| Network behaviour | outbound to the host in DATABASE_URL, and nowhere else |
| Replacement possibility | the SQLite dialect, which is the default and needs no driver at all (node:sqlite) |

### `@scure/bip39` 2.4.0 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | test-only cross-check of the recovery phrase implementation against an independent one |
| Security relevance | medium: it is the second opinion that would notice a wordlist or checksum mistake in ours |
| Network behaviour | none |
| Replacement possibility | the BIP-39 test vectors alone, which is weaker: they check the cases we chose |

### `@types/libsodium-wrappers-sumo` 0.7.8 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | type definitions for libsodium |
| Security relevance | none: types are erased |
| Network behaviour | none |
| Replacement possibility | none |

### `@types/node` 22.20.1 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | Node type definitions |
| Security relevance | none: types are erased |
| Network behaviour | none |
| Replacement possibility | none |

### `@types/pg` 8.23.1 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | type definitions for the PostgreSQL driver |
| Security relevance | none: types are erased |
| Network behaviour | none |
| Replacement possibility | none |

### `esbuild` 0.28.2 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | bundling and minifying the client (build time only) |
| Security relevance | high despite being a dev tool: it decides the bytes the browser executes, which is why it is pinned exactly |
| Network behaviour | none during a build; it ships a platform binary that `ignore-scripts=true` never links by script |
| Replacement possibility | no bundler at all — plain ES modules served unbundled, at the cost of many round trips over Tor |

### `jsqr` 1.4.0 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | test-only decoding of the device-linking QR code the client renders |
| Security relevance | low — it never ships, and it proves the code we draw is readable by a real decoder |
| Network behaviour | none |
| Replacement possibility | dropping the assertion, which would leave the QR renderer unverified |

### `typescript` 5.9.3 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | type checking (`npm run typecheck`); nothing is compiled, the runtime strips types itself |
| Security relevance | medium — the type checker is a large part of what the linter deliberately does not duplicate |
| Network behaviour | none |
| Replacement possibility | none wanted; without it `strict` mode stops catching holes |

### `vitest` 4.1.11 — development only

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Purpose | the test runner for every suite under test/ |
| Security relevance | medium — it runs in development and CI only, and never in the production image |
| Network behaviour | none in this configuration: no reporter, no coverage service, no watch server in CI |
| Replacement possibility | node:test, which would work and would cost a rewrite of every suite |
